## Purpose and Scopesvg image

This document describes the high-level architecture of the Contexter system, including its layered design, module organization, and the relationships between command-line interfaces and implementation modules. It covers the system's structural components, their interactions, and the design patterns used to achieve modularity and maintainability.

For detailed information about individual commands and their usage, see [Command Reference](/ray0404/Contexter/5-command-reference). For implementation details of specific modules, see [Module Organization](/ray0404/Contexter/6.2-module-organization). For the shared utility infrastructure, see [Utility Layer (contexter\_utils)](/ray0404/Contexter/6.3-utility-layer-(contexter_utils)).

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md1-61](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L1-L61) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml1-33](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L1-L33) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py1-61](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L1-L61)

---

## High-Level Architecture Overviewsvg image

Contexter implements a three-layer architecture that separates user interface concerns from business logic and shared infrastructure:

**Diagram: Three-Layer System Architecture with Actual Module Names**

The system consists of:

1. **CLI Layer**: 12 command-line entry points defined in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53)
2. **Implementation Layer**: 12 corresponding Python modules containing business logic
3. **Utility Layer**: Single shared module (`contexter_utils.py`) providing common functionality

This architecture ensures:

- Separation between argument parsing and business logic
- Reusability of implementation modules for programmatic access
- Centralized common functionality to avoid code duplication
- Independent testability of each layer

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-37](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L37) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)contexter.egg-info/top\_level.txt1-13](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/contexter.egg-info/top_level.txt#L1-L13)

---

## Three-Layer Design Patternsvg image

### Layer 1: Command-Line Interfacesvg image

The CLI layer is defined through setuptools entry points that map command names to module entry functions:

| Command | Entry Point Definition | Target Module:Function |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `buildcontext` | `'buildcontext=context_builder:main'` | `context_builder.main()` |
| `reconstructor` | `'reconstructor=reconstructor:main'` | `reconstructor.main()` |
| `updatecontext` | `'updatecontext=update_context:main'` | `update_context.main()` |
| `updater` | `'updater=updater:main'` | `updater.main()` |
| `smartupdate` | `'smartupdate=smart_update:main'` | `smart_update.main()` |
| `sanitizecontext` | `'sanitizecontext=sanitize_context:main'` | `sanitize_context.main()` |
| `buildcontexthtml` | `'buildcontexthtml=build_context_html:main'` | `build_context_html.main()` |
| `reconstructorhtml` | `'reconstructorhtml=reconstructor_html:main'` | `reconstructor_html.main()` |
| `updatecontexthtml` | `'updatecontexthtml=update_context_html:main'` | `update_context_html.main()` |
| `updaterhtml` | `'updaterhtml=updater_html:main'` | `updater_html.main()` |
| `md2html` | `'md2html=md2html:main'` | `md2html.main()` |
| `html2md` | `'html2md=html2md:main'` | `html2md.main()` |

Each CLI command is a thin wrapper that:

- Parses command-line arguments using `argparse`
- Delegates to the corresponding implementation module
- Handles top-level error reporting

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md22-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L22-L35)

### Layer 2: Implementation Modulessvg image

Each implementation module is a standalone Python file containing:

- A `main()` function for CLI invocation
- Business logic for the specific operation
- Imports from `contexter_utils` for shared functionality

The modules are registered as top-level modules in the package:

```px-2
build_context_html.py
context_builder.py
contexter_utils.py
html2md.py
md2html.py
reconstructor.py
reconstructor_html.py
sanitize_context.py
smart_update.py
update_context.py
update_context_html.py
updater.py
updater_html.py
```

This flat module structure (as opposed to a nested package structure) simplifies imports and makes each module independently executable.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-37](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L37) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)contexter.egg-info/top\_level.txt1-13](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/contexter.egg-info/top_level.txt#L1-L13)

### Layer 3: Shared Utility Infrastructuresvg image

The `contexter_utils.py` module provides common functionality used across all implementation modules. This centralization:

- Eliminates code duplication
- Ensures consistent behavior (e.g., file parsing, exclusion patterns)
- Provides a single point for dependency management
- Facilitates maintenance and bug fixes

All 12 implementation modules depend on `contexter_utils`, as evidenced by the module organization where it serves as the foundational layer.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py24](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L24-L24) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)contexter.egg-info/top\_level.txt4](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/contexter.egg-info/top_level.txt#L4-L4)

## Module Organization by Functional Areasvg image

The 12 modules naturally group into four functional areas:

**Diagram: Functional Grouping of Modules**

### Build Operations (2 modules)svg image

- `context_builder.py`: Creates Markdown context files from directories
- `build_context_html.py`: Creates HTML context files from directories

Both modules scan directory structures, apply exclusion patterns, and aggregate files into a single output document.

### Reconstruction Operations (2 modules)svg image

- `reconstructor.py`: Parses Markdown context files and rebuilds directory structures
- `reconstructor_html.py`: Parses HTML context files and rebuilds directory structures

Both modules parse context file formats, extract file paths and content, and recreate the original directory hierarchy.

### Update Operations (5 modules)svg image

- `update_context.py`: Generates patches by comparing two Markdown context files
- `updater.py`: Applies patches to Markdown context files
- `smart_update.py`: High-performance patch generation using rsync-based algorithms (recommended)
- `update_context_html.py`: Generates patches from HTML context files
- `updater_html.py`: Applies patches to HTML context files

These modules implement version control functionality, enabling incremental updates without full reconstruction.

### Utility Operations (3 modules)svg image

- `sanitize_context.py`: Fixes AI-generated Markdown to ensure valid context file format (new in v2.0.0)
- `md2html.py`: Converts Markdown files to HTML
- `html2md.py`: Converts HTML files to Markdown

These modules provide format transformation and data sanitization capabilities.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-37](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L37) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md22-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L22-L35)

## Dual-Format Architecturesvg image

Contexter supports two parallel workflows for different use cases:

**Diagram: Dual-Format Workflow Architecture**

### Format-Specific Featuressvg image

| Feature | Markdown (`*.md`) | HTML (`*.html`) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Build | `context_builder.py` | `build_context_html.py` |
| Reconstruct | `reconstructor.py` | `reconstructor_html.py` |
| Update (generate patch) | `update_context.py` | `update_context_html.py` |
| Update (apply patch) | `updater.py` | `updater_html.py` |
| Smart update | `smart_update.py` | ❌ Not available |
| Sanitization | `sanitize_context.py` | ❌ Not available |
| Format conversion | `md2html.py`, `html2md.py` | `md2html.py`, `html2md.py` |

The Markdown workflow includes two features absent from the HTML workflow:

1. **Smart update** (`smart_update.py`): Uses rsync-based algorithms for efficient patch generation
2. **Sanitization** (`sanitize_context.py`): Fixes AI-generated code formatting issues

This suggests Markdown is the primary working format, while HTML serves as a distribution or presentation format.

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py23-37](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L23-L37) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md22-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L22-L35)

## Dependency Structuresvg image

**Diagram: Module Dependency Graph**

### External Dependenciessvg image

The system depends on five external Python libraries, declared in [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29):

| Library | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `markdown` | Markdown parsing and rendering |
| `Pygments` | Syntax highlighting for code blocks |
| `markdownify` | HTML to Markdown conversion |
| `beautifulsoup4` | HTML parsing and manipulation |
| `patch` | Unified diff generation and application |

All external dependencies are accessed through `contexter_utils.py`, which acts as a dependency aggregation point. This means:

- Implementation modules never directly import external libraries
- External library usage is centralized
- Dependency changes require updates only to `contexter_utils.py`
- Testing can mock external dependencies at a single point

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml23-29](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L23-L29) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py10-12](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L10-L12)

---

## Data Flow Architecturesvg image

The system processes three primary data artifacts:

**Diagram: Data Flow Through System Operations**

### Artifact Typessvg image

1. **Project Directory**: Standard filesystem directory structure containing source files
2. **Context File**: Single-file representation of entire project (`.md` or `.html` format)
3. **Patch File**: Differential update file (`.md` or `.html` format)

### Operation Categoriessvg image

| Operation | Input(s) | Output | Modules |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Build | Directory | Context file | `context_builder.py`, `build_context_html.py` |
| Reconstruct | Context file | Directory | `reconstructor.py`, `reconstructor_html.py` |
| Update (generate) | 2× Context files | Patch file | `update_context.py`, `smart_update.py`, `update_context_html.py` |
| Update (apply) | Context file + Patch | Context file | `updater.py`, `updater_html.py` |
| Convert | Context file | Context file | `md2html.py`, `html2md.py` |
| Sanitize | Context file | Context file | `sanitize_context.py` |

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md22-35](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L22-L35)

---

## Entry Point Registrationsvg image

The system's entry points are registered through setuptools configuration:

When the package is installed via `pip install`, setuptools:

1. Creates executable wrapper scripts in the Python environment's `bin/` directory
2. Maps each command name to the specified `module:function` target
3. Makes commands available system-wide (or virtualenv-wide) in the user's PATH

This registration mechanism ensures:

- Commands are accessible from any directory
- No manual PATH manipulation required
- Clean uninstallation removes all command entries
- Standard Python packaging practices are followed

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py39-53](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L39-L53)

---

## Summarysvg image

The Contexter system architecture follows these key principles:

1. **Strict Layering**: CLI, Implementation, and Utility layers with clear separation of concerns
2. **1:1 Mapping**: Each CLI command maps to exactly one implementation module
3. **Centralized Infrastructure**: Single utility module (`contexter_utils.py`) serves all implementation modules
4. **Dual-Format Support**: Parallel Markdown and HTML workflows with format conversion capabilities
5. **Modular Design**: Flat module structure enables independent development and testing
6. **Dependency Aggregation**: External libraries accessed only through utility layer
7. **Standard Packaging**: Setuptools-based distribution with console script entry points

This architecture supports extensibility (add new commands by creating module + entry point), maintainability (changes localized to specific modules), and usability (consistent command-line interface across all tools).

**Sources:** [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)setup.py1-61](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/setup.py#L1-L61) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)pyproject.toml1-33](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/pyproject.toml#L1-L33) [![svg image](data:image/svg+xml;base64,)README.md1-61](https://github.com/ray0404/Contexter/blob/79ebf745/README.md#L1-L61)
